summary: DGHS reports 1,239 new suspected cases in 24 hours, pushing the nationwide cumulative total to over 236,000.

headline_marked: LPG prices in [[Bangladesh rise 52% since February]], far outpacing neighbors
headline: LPG prices in Bangladesh rise 52% since February, far outpacing neighbors
summary: Consumers are paying 30-45% more than official rates in Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Nepal due to supply chain disruptions and structural disadvantages.
details: The official retail price of LPG in Bangladesh has surged by nearly 52% since February, rising from Tk 113 per kg to Tk 171.68 in November. This increase is far higher than the price hikes seen in Pakistan (34%), Sri Lanka (12%), Nepal (6%), and India (7%).

Bangladesh's LPG costs are now roughly 30% to 45% higher than the official retail rates in Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Nepal. While India's household prices are lower due to government subsidies, commercial LPG in Delhi is actually higher than Bangladesh's regulated rate.

The BERC chairman identified three structural disadvantages for Bangladesh: small purchasing volumes, a heavy reliance on spot market purchases, and the additional cost of transferring LPG from mother vessels to smaller vessels.

Supply chain disruptions in the Middle East have worsened the situation. Importers have been forced to shift from Gulf sources to the US, with US-origin imports rising from 27.4% in September 2025 to 85% in September this year.

This shift to US supplies has significantly increased costs. Shipments from the US Gulf take 40-45 days to reach the Bay of Bengal, compared to just two weeks from the Middle East, and freight costs have jumped from $82 to as much as $250 per tonne.
